terminology mismatch: The Nature Of Culture

failures.source: Before going to sleep, you sit in your tent for a while, poring over half-drawn maps and planning the next day's travels. When the lines start to blur on the paper and the humidity begins to weigh down on your mind, you step outside for a spell of fresh air. Almost everyone except for the troops on guard duty have gone to sleep, only the Scholar Carlos Zárraga still sits up, warming his hands by the campfire. As FName2’s rotation ends and FHeShe2 is replaced at FHisHer2 post, FHeShe2 sits down next to the philosopher and starts to remove FHisHer2 armour.
failures.translation: 睡前，你在帐篷里坐了一会儿，埋头研究画到一半的地图，规划明天的行程。纸上的线条渐渐模糊，潮湿的空气也压得你头脑昏沉，于是你走到外面透透气。除了值守的士兵，几乎所有人都已入睡，只有学者卡洛斯·萨拉加还坐在营火旁烤手。随着FName2’s rotation endsFHeShe2 is replaced atFHisHer2 postFHeShe2 sits down next to the philosopher and starts to removeFHisHer2 armour.

failures.source: Carlos smiles, apparently not uneasy about referencing old pagan symbolism.
failures.translation: 卡洛斯微微一笑，显然并不介意提及古老的异教象征。

failures.source: "Does it worry you that I do not pay tribute to your god?"
failures.translation: “你不向你的神进贡，这会让你烦恼吗？”

failures.source: She laughs heartily and jumps on top of you in a swift and elegant movement.
failures.translation: 她开怀大笑，动作迅捷而优雅地扑到你身上。

failures.source: "I am a Christian man by birth, and nothing will ever change that, but I barely pay tribute to the Lord myself."
failures.translation: “我生来就是基督徒，这一点永远不会改变，但我自己也很少向上帝进贡。”

failures.source: Coyotl has just finished relating the story of how he once, with a small group of warriors, defeated a large group of Mixtec warriors defending a strategically important village. Allegedly, it involved a night ambush, a bold distraction, and a not insignificant amount of hilarious quips.
failures.translation: 科约特尔刚讲完一个故事：他曾带着一小队战士，击败了守卫一座战略要地村庄的大批米斯特克战士。据说那场战斗有夜袭、大胆的声东击西，还有不少妙语连珠，着实令人捧腹。

failures.source: "Well, of course I've had superiors, but as an Eagle Warrior, I have always been in charge of the men I fought with."
failures.translation: “嗯，我当然有过上级，但作为鹰战士，我一直负责指挥和我并肩作战的弟兄们。”

failures.source: "You /are/ a remarkable woman, PNameFirst. Decisive, courageous... beautiful. A woman commanding troops on the field of battle is quite unheard of in Aztec society."
failures.translation: “你/是/位出众的女人，PNameFirst。果断、勇敢……美丽。在阿兹特克社会，女人率军上战场可是闻所未闻。”

failures.source: "I think I'll make a quick round of the guard posts before I go to bed. I sleep better when I know that everything is in order."
failures.translation: “睡觉前，我想去各个哨岗巡查一圈。知道一切都井然有序，我才能睡得踏实。”

failures.source: "Of course, Capitán. I think I'll make a quick round of the guard posts myself, before I go to bed. I sleep better when I know that everything is in order."
failures.translation: “当然，队长。我想睡前也去各个哨岗巡查一圈。我知道一切都安排妥当，才能睡得踏实。”

failures.source: "This flower grows only in a few holy sites, near the peaks of tall mountains. They grow despite the roughness of the soil, and they endure despite the harsh winds and the low temperatures at such altitudes."
failures.translation: “这种花只生长在几处圣地，靠近高山之巅。即便土壤贫瘠，它们也能生长；即便高海拔处狂风凛冽、气温低寒，它们也能挺过来。”

failures.source: He extends the flower to you.
failures.translation: 他把花递给你。

failures.source: "This is exactly the kind of thing I'm talking about! We work for the King of Spain, these are inferior people, centuries behind our culture and our sciences! That savage has no place in this expedition, and you choose to defend FHimHer2 instead of doing what's right! If you don't do something soon, Capitán, I will be forced to take matters into my own hands!"
failures.translation: 这正是我说的那种事！我们为西班牙国王效力，这些人低我们一等，文化和科学都落后了几个世纪！那个野蛮人不该加入远征队，你却选择袒护FHimHer2，而不主持公道！队长，如果你再不采取行动，我就只能亲自解决这件事了！

failures.source: "You /cannot/ ask us to compromise our convictions and ignore the threat that these savages pose when we let them into our midst! Every man is entitled to defend himself from danger, and if you don't address this problem, I will be forced to take matters into my own hands!"
failures.translation: 你/不能/要求我们违背信念，对那些被我们接纳进来后可能带来的威胁视而不见！每个人都有权保护自己免受危险。你若不解决这个问题，我就只能亲自出手了！

failures.source: "Capitán, you cannot let this slide! Self-defence or not, FName2 is not one of us, and FHeShe2 has slain a soldier of Spain! You have to make FHimHer2 leave."
failures.translation: 队长，你不能就这么算了！不管是不是自卫，FName2都不是我们的人，而FHeShe2杀了西班牙士兵！你必须让FHimHer2离开。

failures.source: "We were married! How /dared/ you lay a hand on FHimHer2?!"
failures.translation: “我们结过婚！你怎么/敢/对FHimHer2动手？！”

failures.source: After assigning tasks to your people, you set off with three of your troops to patrol the area and make sure it hides no unpleasant surprises. You find yourself walking alongside Federico Quintero, who is silent as usual. The jungle seems quiet beyond the usual ambience of birds and insects, and a little conversation wouldn't endanger the patrol.
failures.translation: 给队员们分派好任务后，你带着三名士兵出发巡查周边，确保没有什么意外状况。你发现自己正与费德里科·金特罗并肩而行，他一如既往地沉默。丛林里除了鸟鸣虫叫，显得格外安静；聊上几句也不会妨碍巡逻。

failures.source: "I've done really terrible things, FNameFirst2. I was the lowest kind of person you can imagine. I had /nothing/."
failures.translation: “我做过非常可怕的事，FNameFirst2。我曾经是你能想象到的最卑劣的人。我一无所有。”

failures.source: While setting up camp for the night, a commotion calls your attention to a small group of your people who are gathered next to a half-erected tent. FName1 and FName2 are shouting angrily at each other, with a few of your other people trying to keep them from getting physical. It seems that the animosity between them has been slowly developing for some time, and has finally come to a head over something as inconsequential as the proximity of their tents.
failures.translation: 夜里扎营时，一阵骚动引起了你的注意。一小群部下聚在一顶只搭了一半的帐篷旁。FName1和FName2正怒气冲冲地互相叫骂，另有几名部下试图拦住他们，免得双方动起手来。看来他们之间的嫌隙已经逐渐积累了一段时间，最终因为两顶帐篷离得太近这种微不足道的小事彻底爆发了。

failures.source: At the sound of your voice, everybody involved immediately snaps to attention. You scold FNameLast1 and FNameLast2, attempting to rouse their sense of duty to the Spanish crown and shame them for their dishonourable conduct, but your words seem to fall a little flat. You can't quite speak to these men in a way that puts them in their place and rekindles their pride and loyalty to the mission. When you're done speaking to your troops, you get the sense that you haven't really achieved anything. In an attempt to remedy this failure, you assign FNameLast1 and FNameLast2 to latrine duty tonight and dismiss everyone.
failures.translation: 听到你的声音，在场所有人立刻立正。你斥责FNameLast1和FNameLast2，试图唤起他们对西班牙王室的责任感，并让他们为自己的不光彩行为感到羞愧，可你的话似乎没什么效果。你没能让这些人服服帖帖，也没能重新点燃他们对这次任务的自豪与忠诚。训话结束后，你觉得自己并没有真正解决问题。为了弥补这次失败，你罚FNameLast1和FNameLast2今晚去清理厕所，然后让众人散去。

failures.source: At the sound of your voice, everybody involved immediately snaps to attention. You demand an explanation of this disorderly spectacle, and both people involved give you their side of the story. There really does seem to be little more to it than a natural, unfounded animosity between two comrades in arms. Nevertheless, you decide that the loyalty of FName1 is most important to you right now, so you find a reason to take FHisHer1 side in the matter and assign FNameLast2 to latrine duty for the night. The rest of your men don't seem to identify the underlying favouritism, so you dismiss everyone and leave them to finish setting up the camp.
failures.translation: 听到你的声音，在场所有人立刻立正。你要求他们解释这场混乱的闹剧，双方各自讲述了事情经过。看来这不过是两名战友之间自然而然、毫无根据的敌意。不过，你此刻最看重FName1的忠诚，于是找了个理由站在FHisHer1一边，并罚FNameLast2晚上去清理厕所。其他部下似乎没有察觉你偏袒其中一方，于是你让众人散去，任由他们继续扎营。

failures.source: At the sound of your voice, everybody involved immediately snaps to attention. You demand an explanation of this disorderly spectacle, and both people involved give you their side of the story. There really does seem to be little more to it than a natural, unfounded animosity between two comrades in arms. Nevertheless, you decide that the loyalty of FName2 is most important to you right now, so you find a reason to take FHisHer2 side in the matter and assign FNameLast1 to latrine duty for the night. The rest of your men don't seem to identify the underlying favouritism, so you dismiss everyone and leave them to finish setting up the camp.
failures.translation: 听到你的声音，在场所有人立刻立正。你要求他们解释这场混乱的闹剧，双方各自讲述了事情经过。看来这不过是两名战友之间自然而然、毫无根据的敌意。不过，你此刻最看重FName2的忠诚，于是找了个理由站在FHisHer2一边，并罚FNameLast1晚上去清理厕所。其他部下似乎没有察觉你偏袒其中一方，于是你让众人散去，任由他们继续扎营。

failures.source: Isabela is chopping firewood for tonight's campfire when you pass by her. She pauses and folds her hands on top of the axe.
failures.translation: 你经过时，伊莎贝拉正在劈今晚篝火要用的柴。她停下动作，双手叠放在斧柄上。

failures.source: "I will not enjoy it, but it must be done. The rebels sow dissent among the Taíno, who are a peaceful people by nature. They exploit the negro slaves we've brought here, and they kill innocent people and burn down Taíno huts and Spanish houses alike. They claim to fight for freedom and justice, but they have their own petty interests at heart."
failures.translation: “我不会享受这个过程，但这是必须做的。叛军在泰诺人中散播不和，而泰诺人天性平和。他们还剥削我们带来的黑人奴隶，杀害无辜百姓，烧毁泰诺人的茅屋和西班牙人的房屋。他们声称自己是为自由与正义而战，心里盘算的却是自己的那点私利。”

failures.source: "She was a proud and gracious woman, but she held no special status within her tribe. She lived in the village in the jungle in the eastern part of the island. The tribe cast her out for falling in love with my father, and she came to live with him in Santo Domingo. The Spanish disease claimed her when I was 9 years old."
failures.translation: “她是位骄傲而和蔼的女人，在部族里却没有什么特殊地位。她住在岛屿东部丛林中的一个村庄。部族因为她爱上我父亲而将她逐出，她便来到圣多明各与父亲同住。我九岁那年，她染上西班牙人带来的疾病，最终病逝了。”

failures.source: "What's this?! Chorizo, my brothers and sisters! Genuine Spanish chorizo! How have you come into possession of this, Maestro?"
failures.translation: “这是什么？！西班牙辣香肠，我的兄弟姐妹们！正宗的西班牙辣香肠！大师，你是怎么弄到它的？”

failures.source: "It is my secret weapon from the village of Guijuelo. Go on, put it in the stew."
failures.translation: “这是我从吉胡埃洛村带来的秘密武器。来吧，把它放进炖菜里。”

failures.source: You get the distinct sense that he's concealing something from you, but it seems like the conversation is over. You nod and walk off to inspect the guard posts before bed.
failures.translation: 你清楚地感觉到他在对你隐瞒什么，但谈话似乎已经结束。你点点头，起身去检查哨岗，然后准备睡觉。

failures.source: "Though I find imagination to be the spice of life, a basis in true events lends an air of legitimacy to a story, don't you think, mi PSenorSenora? It lets an author transcend the boundaries of his or her own musings to touch on the raw experience of life."
failures.translation: “我觉得想象力是生活的调味料，不过以真实事件为基础，故事才会显得可信。阁下觉得呢？这样一来，作者就能超越自己的种种遐想，触及生活最真实的体验。”

failures.source: "Your Spanish is very good."
failures.translation: “你的西班牙语说得真好。”

failures.source: "Like myself, he wore the black panoply of the Fekete sereg. He will not be difficult to identify if we find him - or his remains."
failures.translation: “和我一样，他也穿着黑色的费凯特军团甲胄。要是我们找到他，或者他的遗骸，不难认出来。”

failures.source: "I harbour no illusions about the dangers of this land. All evidence suggests that a bleak fate befell Gutiérrez's expedition."
failures.translation: “我对这片土地的危险不抱任何幻想。所有迹象都表明，古铁雷斯的远征队遭遇了悲惨的结局。”

failures.source: "I know FNameFirst1 meant a lot to you. I'm proud to serve under a PManWoman who could see past culture and skin colour to fall in love with a native - FHeShe1 was a great warrior and a remarkable FManWoman1."
failures.translation: “我知道FNameFirst1对你意义重大。我很自豪能在一位PManWoman麾下效力，他能超越文化和肤色的隔阂，爱上一位原住民——FHeShe1是一位伟大的战士，也是个了不起的FManWoman1。”

failures.source: "None of us is happy about what happened to FNameFirst1. Believe me, /not one/ of us."
failures.translation: “我们谁都不为FNameFirst1遭遇的事感到高兴。相信我，我们每个人都不是。”

failures.source: "/Dios mio FManWoman2/, will you ever run out of vapid clichés?!"
failures.translation: “/我的天FManWoman2/，你这空洞的陈词滥调什么时候才说得完？！”

failures.source: Glory of the Wilderness
failures.translation: 荒野之荣
diagnostics: R0013667_6532ee628f: terminology mismatch ['Glory of the Wilderness']
terminology mismatch: Glory of the Wilderness

failures.source: FNameFirst1 nods pensively, staring into the crackling camp fire; FHeShe1 smiles.
failures.translation: FNameFirst1若有所思地点点头，凝望着噼啪作响的营火；FHeShe1笑了。

failures.source: FHeShe1 frowns and stares pensively into the crackling camp fire.
failures.translation: FHeShe1皱起眉头，若有所思地凝望着噼啪作响的营火。

failures.source: FHeShe1 stares into the crackling camp fire. Then FHeShe1 stands up and brushes the sand off FHisHer1 pants.
failures.translation: FHeShe1凝望着噼啪作响的营火。随后，FHeShe1站起身，拍去FHisHer1裤子上的沙土。

failures.source: "One day, he approached myself and a colleague about a different kind of work. We had a bit of a reputation for ruthlessness, you see - in truth, I simply wanted to please my lord so as to advance in my station."
failures.translation: “有一天，他找我和一位同僚谈另一种差事。您懂的，我们以心狠手辣闻名——说实话，我只是想讨好主上，好让自己步步高升。”

failures.source: "I know, mi PSenorSenora. This is why I have kept my story to myself until now."
failures.translation: “我明白，阁下。所以我一直把这段往事藏在心里，直到今天才说出来。”

failures.source: "The fourth one was the end for me. There was a slight inaccuracy in the Count's plan. Nothing he could have predicted, and we failed to improvise our way out of it. People died who didn't have to die, among them my partner. I was apprehended and put to the question. In the end they broke me, and though I knew what would happen, through the pain, the name of my lord slipped from my lips."
failures.translation: “第四次差事彻底毁了我。伯爵的计划有个小小的疏漏。他不可能预料到会发生那种事，而我们也没能临机应变、脱身而出。有些人本不必死，却还是死了，我的搭档也在其中。我被抓住，遭到审讯。最终他们击垮了我；尽管我知道后果会是什么，疼痛之中，我还是说出了主上的名字。”

failures.source: "It's okay if you don't want to talk about it. I just thought being the Capitán must get lonely, that's all. I'm glad you have Citlalli to lean on, even if she's a stranger to our culture."
failures.translation: “不想说也没关系。我只是觉得，身为队长一定很孤独，仅此而已。幸好有西特拉利可以依靠，尽管她和我们的文化格格不入。”

failures.source: "We seem to be doing all right so far. With your leadership, I'm sure we'll find our way home with a ship full of gold and plenty of stories to tell."
failures.translation: “目前看来我们还应付得来。有你带领，我相信我们会满载金币、带着许多故事，乘船平安回家。”

failures.source: "Do you think your father would be proud of us?"
failures.translation: 你觉得父亲会为我们感到骄傲吗？

failures.source: "Who knows what would make the old man proud."
failures.translation: 谁知道那老头怎样才会感到骄傲。

failures.source: "I’m sure he's proud of /you/. He really had to work hard to keep it bottled up when he saw us off."
failures.translation: 我敢肯定他为/你/感到骄傲。送我们出发时，他可是费了好大劲才没把心里的感情表露出来。

failures.source: "I know he's proud of us all for coming here."
failures.translation: 我知道，他为我们所有人来到这里感到骄傲。

failures.source: "What did I tell you about letting down your guard?"
failures.translation: 我怎么跟你说的？别放松警惕。

failures.source: The FType1 runs off, shouting your orders to the others at the top of FHisHer1 lungs. You quickly grab your weapons and armour and hurry out of the tent. The camp is utter mayhem, tents are ablaze and injured troops and slaves are scattered across the ground. Scouting off into the darkness towards the west, you can see a handful of your troops disappearing into the jungle.
failures.translation: FType1跑开了，扯着嗓子向其他人高喊你的命令。你迅速拿起武器和护甲，冲出帐篷。营地里一片混乱，帐篷燃起大火，受伤的士兵和奴隶散落在地上。你朝西边的黑暗中望去，看见几名部下正消失在丛林里。

failures.source: Half a dozen slaves who took part in the attack have survived, and half a dozen more that didn't fight have been rounded up as well. The slaves are kneeling at the outskirts of the camp, stripped of their stolen weapons and armour. FName4 is overseeing them - FHeShe4 wipes the sweat from FHisHer4 forehead and looks at you wearily.
failures.translation: 参与袭击的奴隶有六人幸存，另有六名没有参战的奴隶也被抓了起来。他们跪在营地边缘，身上被搜走了偷来的武器和护甲。FName4正在看管他们——FHeShe4擦去额头上的汗水，疲惫地看着你。

failures.source: FNameFirst4 draws FHisHer4 sword and signals to the other troops, who begin to systematically dispose of the surviving slaves by running them through one by one. The slaves who didn't take part in the attack cry and plead for their lives, but they are not spared. When the grim work is done, your soldiers carry the corpses into the jungle and toss them in the mud.
failures.translation: FNameFirst4拔出FHisHer4的剑，向其他士兵示意。他们开始逐个刺杀幸存的奴隶。没有参与袭击的奴隶哭喊着乞求饶命，却无人放过他们。残酷的差事结束后，你的士兵把尸体抬进丛林，扔进泥地里。

failures.source: FNameFirst4 draws FHisHer4 sword and signals to the other troops, who summarily dispose of the surviving attackers. The slaves who didn't take part in the attack are set free and ordered to restore the camp to order, the first order of business being to carry the corpses of their rebellious colleagues into the jungle and toss them in the mud.
failures.translation: FNameFirst4拔出FHisHer4的剑，向其他士兵示意，他们随即处决了剩余的袭击者。没有参与袭击的奴隶被释放，并奉命收拾营地；他们首先要把那些叛乱同伴的尸体抬进丛林，扔进泥地里。

failures.source: FNameFirst4 signals to the other troops, who reluctantly set all of the surviving slaves free. The slaves who didn't take part in the attack are ordered to restore the camp to order while the other is sent into the jungle to live or die on their own terms.
failures.translation: FNameFirst4向其他士兵示意。他们虽不情愿，还是释放了所有幸存的奴隶。没有参与袭击的奴隶奉命收拾营地，另一名奴隶则被送进丛林，任其自生自灭。

failures.source: Near the embers of the camp fire, you see Tayanna lying on the ground, sobbing, with her face buried in her hands. Citlalli looms over her, unarmed, anger smouldering in her voice.
failures.translation: 篝火余烬旁，塔娅娜躺在地上啜泣，双手掩面。西特拉利站在她面前，手无寸铁，声音里压着怒火。

failures.source: FNameFirst1 makes FHimHer1self scarce and you seek out the two lovebirds. You find them at a nearby stream, washing their cutlery conspicuously close to each other.
failures.translation: FNameFirst1悄悄离开，你则去找那对恋人。你在附近的小溪边找到了他们，两人洗着餐具，彼此靠得格外近。

failures.source: FNameFirst3 covers FHisHer3 face with FHisHer3 hands and storms off so you won't see FHimHer3 burst into tears. FNameFirst2 rushes after FHimHer3, looking equally devastated.
failures.translation: FNameFirst3用FHisHer3双手捂住FHisHer3的脸，气冲冲地走开，不想让你看见FHimHer3哭出来。FNameFirst2也伤心欲绝地追了上去。

failures.source: The FType1 is out on patrol, and you can raid FHisHer1 tent uninterrupted. True enough, secreted away among FNameFirst1's personal effects, you find items that were clearly stolen from among the Valuables in the supply carts. Just as you make this discovery, FNameLast1 returns from patrol.
failures.translation: FType1正在外出巡逻，你可以趁机搜查FHisHer1的帐篷。果然，你在FNameFirst1的私人物品中发现了显然是从补给车贵重物品里偷来的东西。你刚发现这些赃物，FNameLast1就巡逻回来了。

failures.source: The Treasure Hunters
failures.translation: 寻宝者

failures.source: Although not heavily injured, the men look haggard and weak. At their sides hang swords and arquebuses, and two of the men are carrying a chest between them. You spy a glint of gold from the ajar lid. The leader of the men steps forward to speak.
failures.translation: 这些人伤得不重，却个个面容憔悴、虚弱不堪。他们腰间挂着剑和火绳枪，其中两人合抬着一个箱子。箱盖半开，你瞥见里面有金子闪闪发光。为首的人走上前来开口说话。

failures.source: "My name is Claudio Asturias, I am the leader of this party. We came to the mainland from Santo Domingo not long ago - we stopped off at Fortaleza de Gutiérrez, and from there headed out. We had heard from someone at the fortress of an abandoned temple nearby which held treasure left behind by savages who saw no value in it."
failures.translation: “我叫克劳迪奥·阿斯图里亚斯，是这支队伍的领头人。我们不久前从圣多明各来到美洲大陆，在古铁雷斯要塞停留过，之后便启程出发。我们从要塞里的人口中得知，附近有座废弃神殿，里面留有一批宝藏，是那些不识货的野蛮人留下的。”

failures.source: Claudio gestures at the chest held by his companions. The gold glints invitingly. They don't look like they'd be able to put up a fight if you decided to take it for yourself.
failures.translation: 克劳迪奥指了指同伴手里的箱子。金子诱人地闪着光。看起来，只要你想据为己有，他们根本无力反抗。

failures.source: Claudio and his men quickly hurry off without looking back. You hear them clumsily stumble through the woods as you settle back down at the camp fire.
failures.translation: 克劳迪奥和他的手下匆匆离去，头也不回。你重新在篝火旁坐下时，听见他们在树林里跌跌撞撞、笨手笨脚地穿行。

failures.source: Claudio and his men slowly turn and push back into the forest. You catch a mournful glance backwards from Claudio as you settle back down at the camp fire.
failures.translation: 克劳迪奥和他的手下慢慢转身，重新钻进森林。你重新在篝火旁坐下时，瞥见克劳迪奥满含哀伤地回头望了一眼。

failures.source:
The Alcazar de Colon was built in the period 1510 - 1512 using the slave labour of 1500 natives. It was built with coral rock in a mixture of the Mudejar and Gothic styles (without use of any nails). The palace consisted of about 50 rooms and was the residence of Diego Colon, son of Christopher Columbus, when he was the Viceroy of Española and the Indies.

The Alcazar de Colon played a strategic role in the Spanish conquest and colonisation of America. It was here Cortez, Pizarro, Balboa, and Velasquez planned their conquests of Mexico, Peru, Panama, and Cuba.
failures.translation:
哥伦布宫建于1510年至1512年，使用了1500名原住民奴工。宫殿以珊瑚岩建成，融合了穆德哈尔式与哥特式风格（没有使用任何钉子）。宫内约有50个房间；迭戈·哥伦布是克里斯托弗·哥伦布之子，在担任西班牙岛和印度群岛副王期间曾居住于此。

哥伦布宫在西班牙征服并殖民美洲的过程中发挥了战略作用。科尔特斯、皮萨罗、巴尔博亚和贝拉斯克斯曾在此策划征服墨西哥、秘鲁、巴拿马和古巴。

failures.source:
The Fountain of Youth was first mentioned in the fifth century B.C. by the Greek historian Heroditus, who told about a fountain with a special kind of water in Ethiopia. The fountain crops up through history, both in connection to Alexander the great, in the legends of Al-Khidr, and others.

Through the ages, the tales of the fountain grew, and in the ages of exploration it was said that the land surrounding the fountain contained gold and riches, and that the fountain could make old men young again (presumably old women too).

Caribbean Indians told the European explorers of a land called "Bimini" somewhere to the north, where a fountain could restore old men to their youth and vitality.

Ponce de Leon is the person most commonly linked with the discovery of the Fountain of Youth. He was charged by the Spanish King to find, conquer, and colonise Bimini, and he set forth to look for it in 1513. It is believed that he was primarily looking for gold and slaves, and didn't give much credence to the legends of the fountain. He never mentioned finding the fountain, but because he landed in Florida, the fountain is now thought to be there.
failures.translation:
青春泉最早于公元前5世纪见于希腊历史学家希罗多德的记述。他讲到埃塞俄比亚有一眼泉水，水质十分特别。这眼泉水在历史上屡屡出现，既与亚历山大大帝有关，也见于阿尔希德尔等人的传说。

岁月流转，关于这眼泉水的故事越来越多。到了大航海时代，人们传说泉水周围的土地蕴藏着黄金和财富，而且泉水能让老人重返青春（想必也包括老妇人）。

加勒比原住民曾告诉欧洲探险者，北方某处有一片名为“比米尼”的土地，那里有一眼泉水，能让老人恢复青春与活力。

最常与发现青春泉联系在一起的人是庞塞·德莱昂。西班牙国王命他找到并征服比米尼，将其殖民；1513年，他启程寻找这片土地。据认为，他主要是在寻找黄金和奴隶，并不太相信泉水的传说。他从未提过自己找到过泉水，但由于他在佛罗里达登陆，如今人们便认为泉水在那里。
diagnostics: terminology mismatch: Greek, gold, European, Spanish

failures.source:
The Venezuelan island Cubaqua was discovered in 1498 by Cristopher Columbus. At the time of Columbus' arrival in the new world, sources of gold, pearls and spices were a strong motivation for Spain to expand in the Americas. When Christopher Columbus brought samples of the riches of the Americas back to Spain, many expeditions were formed by explorers and adventurers to seek the riches of the newly discovered lands.

The first Spanish town in the new world was established in Cubaqua in 1528 to serve as a center for gathering pearls. The Spanish organised harvesting programs along the coasts of Venezuela and Colombia and shipped huge quantities of pearls to Europe. The north-east coast of Venezuela became known as "The Pearl Coast".

As a result of the intensive harvesting, the pearl oysters in Venezuela and Colombia had become much scarcer by the end of the 1500s, and as for the pearls of Cubaqua, which had been the island's greatest resource long before the arrival of the Europeans, the peak of its production of pearls was in the period 1508-1520. By the time of 1531, the results of overexploitation were evident.
failures.translation:
委内瑞拉的库巴瓜岛于1498年由克里斯托弗·哥伦布发现。哥伦布抵达新大陆时，黄金、珍珠和香料的来源是西班牙向美洲扩张的重要动力。克里斯托弗·哥伦布将美洲财富的样品带回西班牙后，许多探险家和冒险家纷纷组建远征队，前往新发现的土地寻求财富。

1528年，新大陆的第一个西班牙城镇在库巴瓜岛建立，作为珍珠采集中心。西班牙人在委内瑞拉和哥伦比亚沿岸组织采珠活动，将大量珍珠运往欧洲。委内瑞拉东北海岸因此得名“珍珠海岸”。

由于过度采集，到16世纪末，委内瑞拉和哥伦比亚的珍珠贝已变得稀少。库巴瓜岛的珍珠曾在欧洲人到来很久以前便是岛上最重要的资源，其珍珠产量的鼎盛时期则是1508至1520年。到1531年，过度开发的后果已显而易见。

failures.source:
Santo Domingo is another name for the island Hispaniola, it was called so during the Spanish colonial times, and it has also been the name of the Eastern part of the island in recent times.

It was named after the major city on the Island, the city of Santo Domingo, founded by Christopher Columbus' brother, Bartholomew, in 1496, after the discovery of gold on the south coast of the island. He was at that time governor of the island, appointed by his brother Christopher.

The gold deposits of Hispaniola were just about depleted in 1515 and shortly after that, Hernando Cortes conquered Mexico and the fabulous riches of silver there attracted the Spaniards already residing in Santo Domingo. The island was abandoned and only a few thousand settlers remained, many of them of mixed Spanish/native heritage, making a living by raising livestock to supply the Spanish ships passing by on their way to the richer colonies on the American mainland.
failures.translation:
圣多明各是伊斯帕尼奥拉岛的另一个名称，在西班牙殖民时期便如此称呼；近代以来，它也指该岛东部。

该岛以岛上的主要城市圣多明各命名。这座城市由克里斯托弗·哥伦布的兄弟巴塞洛缪于1496年建立，当时他在岛屿南岸发现了金矿。巴塞洛缪当时是由兄长克里斯托弗任命的岛上总督。

伊斯帕尼奥拉岛的金矿在1515年前后几乎开采殆尽。不久之后，埃尔南多·科尔特斯征服了墨西哥，那里惊人的白银财富吸引了定居圣多明各的西班牙人。岛屿逐渐荒废，只剩下几千名定居者，其中许多人拥有西班牙/本土血统。他们靠饲养牲畜维生，为途经此地、前往美洲大陆更富庶殖民地的西班牙船只提供补给。

failures.source:
The Taíno Indian are a subgroup of the Arawakan Indians, who are thought to have originated in South America before migrating to the Caribbean. When Christopher Columbus arrived to the New World, Taíno Indians inhabited the Greater Antilles (Cuba, Jamaica, Hispaniola, Haiti, and Puerto Rico) in the Caribbean Sea. According to their own myths, the Taíno Indians were created in a cave on Hispaniola.

Taíno society on Hispaniola is believed to have developed between 1100 and 1500 AD. By the time of Columbus's arrival, their society was comprised of about 20 political chiefdoms, each one ruled by a cacique (chief). It is estimated that there were between 30,000 and 50,000 Taínos on Hispaniola when the Spanish arrived.

The Taínos were skilled at agriculture and hunting.  They were also good sailors, fishermen, canoe makers, and navigators. They had no calendar or writing system, and could only count to twenty, using their hands and feet.

The Spaniards expected the Taíno Indians to acknowledge the sovereignty of the king of Spain by payment of gold tribute, to work and supply provisions of food, and to observe Christian ways. The Taínos rebelled most notably in 1511, when several caciques conspired to oust the Spaniards. They were joined in this uprising by their traditional enemies, the Caribs. Their weapons, however, were no match against Spanish horses and firearms and the revolt was soon ended brutally by the Spanish forces of Governor Juan Ponce de León.

By 1514, there were fewer than 4000 Taínos left, and in 1519 a smallpox epidemic is said to have virtually wiped out the rest of the remaining population.
failures.translation:
泰诺印第安人是阿拉瓦克印第安人的一个分支，人们认为他们最初来自南美洲，后来迁往加勒比地区。克里斯托弗·哥伦布抵达新大陆时，泰诺印第安人居住在加勒比海的大安的列斯群岛（古巴、牙买加、伊斯帕尼奥拉岛、海地和波多黎各）。根据他们自己的神话，泰诺人是在伊斯帕尼奥拉岛的一处洞穴中诞生的。

人们认为，伊斯帕尼奥拉岛上的泰诺社会发展于公元1100至1500年间。哥伦布抵达时，他们的社会由约20个政治酋长领地组成，各由一位酋长统治。据估计，西班牙人抵达时，伊斯帕尼奥拉岛上有三万至五万名泰诺人。

泰诺人擅长农业和狩猎，也善于航海、捕鱼、造独木舟和导航。他们没有历法和文字，计数只能数到二十，靠的是手和脚。

西班牙人要求泰诺印第安人承认西班牙国王的主权，缴纳金币贡品，提供劳役和食物补给，并遵循基督教习俗。泰诺人曾多次反抗，其中最著名的一次发生在1511年：几位酋长密谋驱逐西班牙人。泰诺人的宿敌加勒比人也加入了这场起义。然而，他们的武器远非西班牙人的战马和火器之敌，起义很快遭到西班牙军队残酷镇压。军队由总督胡安·庞塞·德莱昂指挥。

到1514年，泰诺人已不足四千；据说，1519年一场天花疫情几乎消灭了剩余人口。

failures.source:
Tenochtitlan was the Aztec capital at the time of the Spanish conquest in 1521, and was one of the largest cities in the world with perhaps as many as 200,000 inhabitants. The city was laid out in a grid divided by a network of streets and canals and was linked to the cities on the shores of the lake by raised causeways. It has been described as a beautiful and impressive city, with huge blue and red pyramids and white palaces.

Tenochtitlan was the political, economic, and religious center of the greatest empire of Precolumbian Mexico, and its great wealth was obtained not only from trade and industry, but also in great part from the spoils and tributes from the regions conquered by the Aztecs.

The Sacred Precinct with room for more than 8000 people was the heart of Tenochtitlan. It was the religious and ceremonial center of both the city and the empire, the most important Aztec gods had their temples there, and there were schools for training of young noblemen for the priesthood, priests' quarters, and ballcourts.

Adjacent to the Sacred Precinct was the royal palace, the homes of the nobles, and the administrative buildings. This area also featured beautiful gardens, zoos, and aviaries.

The common people lived at a distance in neighbourhoods with their own local temples and markets.
failures.translation:
1521年西班牙征服之际，特诺奇蒂特兰是阿兹特克人的首都，也是当时世界上最大的城市之一，人口可能多达二十万。城市按网格布局，街道与运河纵横交错，并以高架堤道连接湖岸各城。它被形容为一座美丽而壮观的城市，拥有巨大的蓝色和红色金字塔，以及白色宫殿。

特诺奇蒂特兰是前哥伦布时期墨西哥最强大帝国的政治、经济和宗教中心。其财富不仅来自贸易和工业，也很大程度上来自阿兹特克人征服各地后掠夺的战利品与贡品。

圣区可容纳八千多人，是特诺奇蒂特兰的核心，也是城市和帝国的宗教与仪式中心。阿兹特克人最重要的神祇都在此设有神庙；这里还有培养年轻贵族成为祭司的学校、祭司住所和球场。

圣区旁是王宫、贵族宅邸和行政建筑。这片区域还设有精美的花园、动物园和鸟舍。

平民住在较远处的街区，那里有各自的地方神庙和集市。

failures.source:
In the middle of the 14th century, the Tlaxcalteca defeated the Teo-Chichimeca and founded a small but powerful empire in the region that now bears their name. They were skilled fighters who followed the god of war and hunting, Camaxtli.

Owing to their military prowess, Tlaxcala was one of the few areas that the Aztecs couldn't subjugate, but the Aztec conquest of the surrounding area cut off Tlaxcala’s commerce. This situation was maintained until the arrival of the Spanish in the early 16th century.

One of the first major cities encountered by the Spanish on their way into Mexico was Tlaxcala. Cortés tried to negotiate a truce so the Spanish army could pass through Tlaxcala, but the Tlaxcalteca didn't understand the Spanish letters brought by envoys from Cempoala, and assumed that the Spaniards and their new Cempoalan allies had come to attack them.

After several battles and raids, resulting in great losses on both sides, the Tlaxcalteca agreed to assist the Spanish rather than having their houses destroyed and their women and children killed. The Tlaxcalteca explained to Cortés that they and the Mexica were old adversaries whose quarrel dated back many years. Cortés used this dispute to his advantage, and convinced the Tlaxcalteca to assist him on his march to Tenochtitlan. In exchange for their support, he promised not to levy taxes on them or confiscate their land.

In 1521 the alliance succeeded, firmly establishing Spanish control of central Mexico.  Afterward, the Tlaxcalteca continued to aid the Spaniards, fighting against other indigenous tribes and settling the newly conquered territories.
failures.translation:
14世纪中叶，特拉斯卡拉人击败了特奥奇奇梅卡人，并在如今以他们命名的地区建立了一个规模虽小却实力强大的帝国。他们是技艺高超的战士，信奉掌管战争与狩猎的神卡马克斯特利。

凭借强大的军事实力，特拉斯卡拉成为阿兹特克人少数未能征服的地区之一；然而，阿兹特克人征服周边地区后，特拉斯卡拉的贸易遭到切断。这种局面一直持续到16世纪初西班牙人到来。

特拉斯卡拉是西班牙人进入墨西哥途中遇到的首批大城市之一。科尔特斯试图谈判停战，以便西班牙军队通过特拉斯卡拉；但特拉斯卡拉人看不懂森波阿拉使者带来的西班牙文信件，误以为西班牙人和新结盟的森波阿拉人是来进攻他们的。

几场战斗和突袭过后，双方都损失惨重。为了避免房屋被毁、妇女儿童遭杀害，特拉斯卡拉人同意援助西班牙人。他们向科尔特斯解释，自己与墨西加人是宿敌，争端由来已久。科尔特斯利用这场纷争说服特拉斯卡拉人协助他进军特诺奇蒂特兰。作为回报，他承诺不向他们征税，也不没收他们的土地。

1521年，这场联盟取得成功，西班牙人由此牢牢控制了墨西哥中部。此后，特拉斯卡拉人继续援助西班牙人，与其他原住民部族作战，并在新征服的领土上定居。
diagnostics: terminology mismatch: god of war, attack

failures.source:
The name Xipe Totec means "Our Lord the Flayed One", and he was usually depicted as a flayed man clad in his own skin.

He was the Aztec god of agriculture, spring, and seasons, and the symbol of the death and rebirth of nature. Xipe Totec was also the god of the east and the patron of gold smiths.

He was called the flayed god, because according to myth, he flayed himself to stimulate growth in both nature and man. When he had shed his skin, he would reappear as a shining, golden god.

Each year in the beginning of spring, he was honoured by human sacrifices. The priests removed the hearts from the victims while they were still alive, then the priests flayed the bodies and put on the skins, which had been coloured yellow. The yellow skins were called teocuitlaquemitl (golden clothes). Other victims were fastened to a frame and killed with arrows. The blood dripping from these sacrifizes symbolised the fertile spring rain. These rituals symbolized the renewal of the earth and the budding of new life.

Xipe Totec was also known by the names Tlatlauhca, Tlatlauhqui Tezcatlipoca ("Red Smoking Mirror") and Youalahuan ("the Night Drinker").
failures.translation:
希佩托特克意为“我们的被剥皮之主”，通常被描绘成一个剥去皮肤、披着自己人皮的人。

他是阿兹特克人的农业、春季与季节之神，也是自然界死亡与重生的象征。希佩托特克还是东方之神和金匠的守护神。

他被称为剥皮之神，因为神话中说，他剥下自己的皮，以促进自然万物与人类的生长。蜕去皮肤后，他会以光辉耀眼的金色神祇形象重现。

每年初春，人们都会以活人祭祀向他致敬。祭司趁受害者还活着时取出他们的心脏，随后剥下尸体的皮并穿在身上；这些皮肤都被染成黄色。黄色皮衣被称为 teocuitlaquemitl（金色衣裳）。另一些受害者则被绑在架子上，用箭射死。祭品滴落的鲜血象征着滋养万物的春雨。这些仪式象征着大地复苏与新生命萌发。

希佩托特克也以 Tlatlauhca、Tlatlauhqui Tezcatlipoca（“红色烟雾之镜”）和 Youalahuan（“夜之饮者”）之名为人所知。
diagnostics: terminology mismatch: Lord, the Flayed One, spring, gold, Tezcatlipoca

failures.source:
Xolotl was known as The Twin or The Lord of the West, and was the god of fire and bad luck. He was Quetzalcoatl's twin, sons of the virgin Coatlicue, and Quetzalcoatl's double. He was the dark personification of Venus, the evening star, and he guarded the sun on its journey through the underworld at night.

He was a dog-like deity, often depicted with ragged ears, and was identified with sickness and physical deformity. He was also sometimes depicted as a skeleton or a man with the head of a dog (dogs were considered filthy and immoral in the Mesoamerican cultures, and likewise, twins were considered a type of deformity).

According to myth, he accompanied Quetzalcoatl to Mictlan, the land of death, to retrieve the bones from those who inhabited the previous world (Nahui Atl) in order to create new life for this world (Nahui Olin), and he assisted Quetzalcoatl in bringing humankind and fire from the underworld.

In another creation myth it was Xolotl who brought a bone to the gods, who sprinkled it with some of their blood and transformed it into a boy and a girl: the first of the human race.
failures.translation:
索洛特尔被称为孪生者或西方之主，是火神和厄运之神。他是处女科亚特利库埃与羽蛇神的双生子，也是羽蛇神的化身。他是金星（也就是昏星）的黑暗化身，夜间守护太阳穿越冥界。

他是一位犬形神祇，常被描绘成耳朵参差不齐的模样，并与疾病和身体畸形联系在一起。有时他也被描绘成骷髅，或长着狗头的人（在中美洲文化中，狗被视为肮脏且不道德的动物；同样，双胞胎也被视为一种畸形）。

神话中，他陪同羽蛇神前往死亡之地米克特兰，取回曾居住在前一个世界（Nahui Atl）中的人们的骨骸，以便为这个世界（Nahui Olin）创造新的生命；他还协助羽蛇神从冥界带来人类与火。

在另一个创世神话中，是索洛特尔将一根骨头带给诸神。诸神将一些自己的血洒在骨头上，使它化作一男一女，成为人类最初的祖先。
